title: Progressive fidelity handoff and KV sentinel checkpointing for OOM resilience
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: transient GPU OOMs occur during bursty long-context workloads where KV cache growth + peak batch windows exceed headroom. Existing strategies (aggressive eviction, single-model fallback) either cause sudden quality cliffs or high latency retries. Goal: implement a low-latency, graceful OOM recovery path that (1) records lightweight KV checkpoints (sentinels) to enable fast rewind, (2) performs progressive-fidelity handoffs (micro-model / quantized variants with preserved prefix coherence), and (3) coordinates a short kernel-cooldown + slot-based admission to reduce repeated OOMs. The solution should integrate with continuous batching and the admission controller so we avoid global circuit breakers and instead prefer per-request graceful degradation and retry with minimal client-visible regression.
acceptance_criteria: KV sentinel checkpointing stores a compact checkpoint of hot KV entries within 5ms without blocking the main request path
On OOM, requests can rewind to last sentinel and retry with reduced fidelity variant within 200ms median extra latency
End-to-end P95 latency increase <= 30% for degraded retries compared to baseline success path
System-level OOM rate reduced by >= 60% under synthetic burst tests (see benchmark links)
Integration tests covering sentinel restore, progressive handoff, and admission backoff added to runtime CI

2026-02-12 - Diego Ramos: Spike notes - implemented a prototype sentinel that serializes 1) hot KV keys (approx top-5%) and 2) a compact fingerprint of KV values (Bloom-filter-esque) to allow fast restore checks. Prototype added to branch feat/kv-sentinel-spike. Measured serialization cost ~3-6ms on p4d with 14GB KV size (hotset).

2026-02-18 - Eng sync: Decided on multi-stage handoff policy: (A) fast micro-quant model (4-bit quantized, fewer heads) for immediate retry, (B) mid-fidelity dequantized small-model if memory reclaims, (C) full model restore from sentinel when slot leash indicates stable headroom. Avoid full model swap on every OOM to reduce tail latency. See architecture doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/KV+Sentinel+and+Fidelity+Handoff

2026-02-22 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1742 (kv sentinel checkpoint + restore API). PR includes a new kernel-safe checkpoint call that runs in-line at admission boundaries. Requesting reviews from @linnea and @omar. CI currently failing on a flaky restore unit test (race on KV update).

2026-03-01 - Benchmarking: synthetic workload test harness (scripts/perf/oom_burst.sh) results: baseline OOM rate 12% under 3x normal tail bursts; with sentinel + progressive handoff enabled OOM rate dropped to 3.8% and overall per-request median additional latency 110ms for retried flows. We trade some quality for availability (quantized micro-model BLEU drop ~6%) — acceptable for non-SLA critical customers. Detailed numbers: https://drive.redwood.ai/perf/oom_burst_results_20260301.csv

2026-03-05 - Design review: PM (Samir Cho) asked for explicit config knobs per customer: max_retries, fidelity_budget, and sentinel_frequency. Agreed to expose these in Dedicated/Private as advanced controls, and keep conservative defaults for Hosted. Also flagged audit logging and telemetry requirements for QA.

2026-03-08 - Engineering note: Implemented kernel cooldown window (configurable 250ms) that pauses new batch assignments to a GPU for short defrag and async reclaim operations. Observed a ~18% reduction in immediate re-OOM events in end-to-end runs. Need to validate under multi-tenant Dedicated pools.

2026-03-10 - Security/Compliance: Asked security to review sentinel content to ensure no PII is persisted by checkpoints. Added a scrub step that hashes KV keys and filters values above a configured size. Security review ticket: SEC-1346 (in progress).
